question:
I am handing over a finished system to a client whose in-house team will keep developing it after delivery. Besides the program itself, what written material should I prepare for the client, for its end users and for my own organization, and for how long should it be retained?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
I have all the SWEBOK passages I need. Here is the complete set of guidelines, drawn exclusively from what was retrieved.

---

## Documentation to Prepare at System Handover

### A — Documentation for the Client's Development Team (the future maintainers)

**1. Provide the functional specifications to whoever takes ownership of the source code.**
When the client acquires ownership of the source code or the right to modify it, you must supply [SWEBOK excerpt 8aa987ac79340648146a].
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt 48895c1d3102a8915751] [SWEBOK excerpt 138b0c77c0da8e454cc7]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md`)

**2. Hand over all software configuration items (SCIs), including design documentation, test materials, and installation and maintenance documentation.**
Everything that could need to be changed or controlled under configuration management must be identified and transferred: plans, specifications, [SWEBOK excerpt 5821a553bb70a19ff0e7].
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt ae8c53959623d22d6586]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management and Change Control/Software Configuration Items Selection and Change Recording.md`)

**3. Record and hand over the design rationale, including assumptions, alternatives considered, and trade-off criteria.**
The reasons for design decisions may be obvious to the original team but not to those who will modify or maintain the system. [SWEBOK excerpt 312998563ac0c4374b7a] product's long-term maintainability.
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt 7599a55dbdd51a176f9e] long-term maintainability."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Recording Design Rationale for System Maintainability.md`)

**4. Prepare a software maintenance plan that specifies [SWEBOK excerpt 2a01d0619f3b482a5266].**
[SWEBOK excerpt c7977df8cabbd7c6a141] (not after delivery). It should address scope of maintenance, adaptation of processes and tools, identification of the maintenance organisation, and an estimate of costs.
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt dcd77385d2336dc761c2]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Software Maintenance_ Organization, Configuration, and Quality/Software Maintenance Planning and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance Planning and Cost Estimation.md`)

**5. Prepare a concept of operations (CONOPS) or operations plan describing how software modifications will be requested and problems reported.**
This document is a companion to the maintenance plan from the operations perspective and should cover scope, processes, tools, the operations organisation, and cost estimates.
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt 5f0cfd617fd84681199d]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Testing, Operations, and Maintenance/Software Operations and Maintenance Practices/Software Engineering Operations Planning and CONOPS Development.md`)

**6. Include a Software Bill of Materials (SBOM) and a version description document (VDD) with the delivered release.**
The VDD documents the physical contents of the release. The SBOM lists the artifacts included in the build and is an important configuration-management output.
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt 1bc7457ba6b688fca089])."* and *"[SWEBOK excerpt 450578f233490c4cd9fa]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Software Release Management and Deployment Processes.md`)

**7. Deliver release notes describing new capabilities, known problems, and platform requirements, together with installation or upgrade instructions.**
Release notes and installation instructions are part of the standard release package. In some cases, tracking the product's distribution to customers or target systems is also necessary.
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt d68736af96e13ab6f7ad]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Configuration Management Planning and Implementation/Software Configuration Management Tools and Processes/Release Management Tools and Documentation Requirements.md`)

**8. Maintain and transfer requirements documentation so the inheriting team can assess the impact of future changes.**
Requirements documentation serves throughout the service life to communicate intent to engineers who maintain code but were not its original authors. Without it, maintainers cannot determine what the code is *intended* to do, which is essential for identifying defects.
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt 9fa729cde30c7ec98d8b] [SWEBOK excerpt f5db2f00281c4ad98d35]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Requirements_ Foundations and Engineering Practices/Software Requirements Engineering Fundamentals/Software Requirements Documentation and Management Throughout Service Life.md`)

---

### B — Documentation for End Users and Operations Personnel

**9. Provide information that lets users determine whether the software meets their needs, and describe safe and unsafe uses.**
For external stakeholders, documentation must include [SWEBOK excerpt a73cc6bcd1c143c92c62], a description of safe and unsafe use, and clear identification of warnings and critical procedures.
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt 2ec8a6827d0553fc6501]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md`)

**10. Document how users can protect sensitive information created or stored by the software.**
This is a distinct and mandatory item in user-facing documentation: an [SWEBOK excerpt 0d45389c08edc01f9a01].
(source: same file as guideline 9 above — *"[SWEBOK excerpt cdf19b1e62ffd9c64fa3]."*)

**11. Produce user manuals and other written products requested by the customer or required by generally accepted practice.**
Written products that may be required include source code, project plans, requirements documents, risk analyses, design documents, test plans, **user manuals**, technical reports, evaluations, and justifications. All written [SWEBOK excerpt e6878816db2fff24cfe3].
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt 953081cb84d57a99af31]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Collaboration, Communication, and Cognition in Software Engineering/Writing and Communication in Software Engineering.md`)

---

### C — Documentation for Your Own Organisation

**12. Internally retain the requirements specification, design documents, details of tools used, test specifications and results, and details of the methods adopted.**
Your development organisation's internal documentation corpus should include all of these items, as well as a record of problems encountered during the development process.
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt cd4bc952e5f9589c89ef]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md`)

**13. Document significant risks and trade-offs encountered during the project.**
Relevant facts, significant risks and trade-offs, and warnings of undesirable or dangerous consequences from use or misuse must be documented.
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt 6d13321d3ba49220af02]."* — same file as guideline 12 above)

**14. Conduct a project closure process, document stakeholder acceptance, record any known problems, and archive all project materials according to agreed rules.**
Closure processes should involve relevant stakeholders and document their acceptance. Any known problems should be documented. After closure, project materials must be archived in accordance with stakeholder-agreed rules covering archival methods, location, duration, and destruction of sensitive information.
(source: *"Closure [SWEBOK excerpt 43fd4cd61e6b9cb5da09]. [SWEBOK excerpt f9addc8db2ee15e26b56]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Quality Management and Project Oversight/Software Measurement and Organizational Learning/Project Closure and Archival Procedures.md`)

---

### D — Retention Period

**15. Keep all documents for at least the full life cycle of the software product, or for as long as organisational or regulatory requirements demand—whichever is longer.**
This is the single explicit retention rule given in the SWEBOK. It applies to all documents across all audiences listed above.
(source: *"[SWEBOK excerpt 3195bf83cb2eca8378f7]."* — `/workspace/swebok-v4/root/Professional Practice and Collaboration in Software Engineering/Professional Responsibility and Intellectual Property in Software Engineering/Documentation and Requirements Trade-off Management/Documentation Standards and Requirements for Software Engineers.md`)

---

**A note on scope:** The SWEBOK passages retrieved cover the documentation categories above but do not specify formats, page-count requirements, or audience-specific retention differentiation beyond the single rule in Guideline 15. Any further specificity on those points would have to come from the applicable ISO/IEC/IEEE standards cited within the SWEBOK (e.g., ISO/IEC/IEEE 14764 for maintenance, ISO/IEC/IEEE 12207 for lifecycle processes) rather than from the SWEBOK text itself.
